A cancer diagnosis can bring fear, sadness, and uncertainty about what comes next. Our oncology team is here to walk beside you with compassion, clarity, and thoughtful guidance—helping you understand your options while honoring what matters most to you and your pet.
Led by Dr. Kelvin Kow,
New Hampshire’s only full-time, locally based board-certified veterinary oncologist
, our veterinary oncology service in Stratham, NH provides consistent, collaborative cancer care from diagnosis through every stage of your pet’s journey. We combine advanced, evidence-based medicine with a deeply personal approach, making every recommendation with honesty, collaboration, and respect for your pet’s quality of life.
We provide comprehensive cancer care for pets across Stratham, Exeter, Portsmouth, and the greater Seacoast region—ensuring you never have to navigate this journey alone.

Cancer Care FAQs
Get the answers you need from our veterinary oncologly team.
What is a veterinary oncologist?
A veterinary oncologist is a veterinarian who has completed advanced specialty training and board certification in the diagnosis and treatment of cancer in animals. Veterinary oncologists work closely with primary care veterinarians and other specialists to develop individualized treatment plans for pets with cancer.
Does a cancer diagnosis mean my pet will suffer?
Not necessarily. Many pets with cancer continue to enjoy an excellent quality of life for months or even years following diagnosis. Our primary goal is always to maintain or improve quality of life while treating the disease.
Will chemotherapy make my pet sick?
Most pets tolerate chemotherapy much better than people do. Veterinary chemotherapy protocols are designed with quality of life as the priority. Approximately 80% of pets experience few or no significant side effects. If side effects do occur, they are typically mild and temporary.
How do I know if treatment is the right choice for my pet?
Every family and every patient is different. During your consultation, we will discuss the diagnosis, prognosis, treatment options, expected outcomes, costs, and quality-of-life considerations so that you can make the decision that feels right for your pet and your family.
What treatment options are available for pets with cancer?
Depending on the diagnosis, treatment options may include surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, electrochemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapies, palliative or comfort-focused care, or a combination of approaches. Some cancers may also be monitored without immediate treatment.
What is electrochemotherapy?
Electrochemotherapy is a treatment that uses brief electrical pulses to help chemotherapy enter cancer cells more effectively. It can be an excellent option for select tumors and may be used alone or alongside surgery and other treatments.
What is my pet's prognosis?
Prognosis varies widely depending on the type of cancer, stage of disease, and treatment pursued. Some cancers can be cured, while others can often be managed successfully for months or years. During your consultation, we will discuss the expected outcomes and treatment goals specific to your pet’s diagnosis.
How will we know if my pet's quality of life is still good?
Quality of life is one of the most important factors we consider when making treatment recommendations. We will discuss what to monitor at home and help you assess your pet’s comfort, appetite, activity level, and overall happiness throughout treatment.
What should I expect during my pet's first oncology appointment?
The initial consultation typically includes a review of medical records, discussion of diagnostic findings, a physical examination, and a detailed conversation about treatment options and prognosis. Additional diagnostics may be recommended depending on the diagnosis.
Will my primary veterinarian remain involved in my pet's care?
Absolutely. We believe in collaborative care and work closely with your family veterinarian throughout diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up care.
How much does cancer treatment cost?
The cost of treatment varies considerably depending on the diagnosis, recommended therapies, and treatment goals. We provide detailed estimates and discuss costs openly so families can make informed decisions.
Can cancer be cured in pets?
Some cancers can be cured, particularly when diagnosed early and treated aggressively. In other cases, our goal is to achieve long-term control of the disease while maintaining an excellent quality of life.
Is treatment always necessary?
No. There are situations where monitoring, palliative care, or hospice-focused management may be the most appropriate choice. Our role is to help you understand all available options and support whatever decision is best for your pet and family.
How quickly should my pet be seen after a cancer diagnosis?
While some cancers require prompt attention, most diagnoses allow enough time to gather information and discuss treatment options thoughtfully. If your pet has been diagnosed with cancer, we encourage scheduling a consultation as soon as practical.
Why choose specialty oncology care?
With more than 20 years of experience in veterinary oncology, Dr. Kelvin Kow provides advanced cancer care while maintaining a strong focus on quality of life, clear communication, and individualized treatment recommendations. Every treatment plan is tailored to the unique needs of the patient and family, helping pet owners make informed decisions with confidence.
